questions: Given this geometry is the best measured design, which controller-side limit (the controller's response to excursions, not geometry) is the main cause of the off-track endings on the s-bend and oval?
Is there any geometry in this design that you think constrains the controller more than the others, such as the 0.03 m lead or the 0.10 m wheel track?
Where does the first off-track event occur (track, bend, progress, time)? Use per-step telemetry if available.

intent: Final design: the best-measured geometry from Iteration 1, unchanged. Across all tested variants, no single geometry change beat it, and every tested change either cut progress or left it flat. Holding it fixed gives the most reliable result on the final race and the unseen track. Expected: a score near 114, with oval progress near 0.47 and s-bend progress near 0.26, and all runs still ending off track.
learning: Across eleven iterations the largest geometry gain came from the first drivetrain change (radius 0.035, track 0.10, mass 0.6, length 0.14), and every later isolated test has either matched it or lost. Sensor lead peaks near 0.03 m, footprint near 12 mm, array near 5 sensors at ±0.05 m, wheel_track near 0.10 m, and mass near 0.6 kg. The remaining shortfall is the excursion response, which points to the controller rather than the geometry.
rationale: This is the final iteration, and the design written here is the one that races, and it is the basis for the unseen-track race. Across eleven iterations no geometry has beaten Iteration 1 (score 114.39, oval progress 0.47, s-bend progress 0.26). Every run ended off track, and max_error sat at 0.061 to 0.068 m against the 0.06 m floor. The sensor layout (5 sensors, 0.025 m spacing, ±0.05 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.03 m lead) was the best tested. The 7-sensor 16 mm array dropped oval progress to 0.23, the 8 mm array gave 0.41, and lead 0.02 m or 0.04 m both scored lower. On the drivetrain, wheel_track 0.10 beat 0.09 (113.36) and 0.11 (107.60). Mass 0.6 beat 0.8 (105.98) and 0.5 (103.70). Iteration 4 (radius 0.04, mass 0.5, length 0.12) overshot, so the lighter, faster direction did not help. Body width cannot improve the off-track limit, since the 0.06 m floor governs. Changing geometry now would be untested, and the evidence says the remaining gains lie in the controller, which I do not design. So I return the exact Iteration 1 geometry as the best-measured design. The expected result is about 114, matching its measured score, with no new risk on the unseen track.
